why: Yakama Nation visitor window is not a fixed Jul 1-Oct 1; it is set yearly (2020 mid-Sep-Oct 2, 2021 Aug 30-Oct 1 day use only, 2026 Jul 17-Sep 8 with dry camping). Fee is $20/vehicle/day at the Mirror Lake fee box; NW Forest Pass not valid.

best_season.from: Summer, inside the Yakama Nation's visitor window for the Bird Creek side (historically about July 1 to October 1, and shorter in some years); earlier in that window holds more snow.
best_season.to: Summer, during the Yakama Nation’s short visitor window for the Bird Creek side; the Nation sets the dates each year, recently anywhere from mid-July to October 1 and sometimes only about a month long, so confirm before planning. Earlier in the window holds more snow.

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow.from: Late August through September, while the Yakama Nation opens the Bird Creek side to visitors; earlier holds more snow
seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow.to: August and September, while the Yakama Nation has the Bird Creek side open to visitors (the dates change each year); earlier holds more snow

to.reason: The headwall carries its best snow, but the reservation side opens mid-July in some years and not until late August in others.
Usually inside the visitor window at least part of the month; the headwall still holds snow though crevasses below Sunrise Camp open up.
Firm snow or ice on the headwall and open crevasses; the visitor window has closed as early as the first week in some years, so check the dates.
The reservation area is closed to visitors by October in recent years, and early storms ice the headwall.

approach.from: Start from the Bird Creek Road trailhead (~5,700 ft) on the Yakama Reservation side; route-finding across moraines and glacier fields begins around 6,700 ft, reaching Sunrise Camp at 8,300 ft.
approach.to: Start from the Bird Creek Road trailhead (~5,700 ft) on the Yakama Reservation side; route-finding across moraines and glacier fields begins around 6,700 ft, reaching Sunrise Camp at 8,300 ft. The Yakama Nation decides each year whether overnight stays are allowed, so plan a single-day push in day-use-only years.

access.fees.to: $20 per vehicle per day Yakama Nation day-use fee for the Bird Creek side (cash or check, at the Mirror Lake fee box); camping, in years it is allowed, is charged per night on top. Northwest Forest Pass and Discovery Pass are not valid here.

access.permit.from: Yakama Indian Reservation Tract-D tribal-use permit required to start from Bird Creek Meadows.
access.permit.to: Yakama Nation Tract D day-use permit required to start from Bird Creek Meadows; pay at the fee box at Mirror Lake.

access.closures.from: Non-tribal-member season restricted to roughly July 1–October 1; the Mazama Glacier route and Bird Creek Meadows are among the few reservation-side areas open to public recreation.
access.closures.to: Closed to non-tribal visitors outside a short summer window the Yakama Nation sets each year; recent windows have opened between mid-July and mid-September and closed between early September and October 1.

from.what: Yakama Nation Tract D recreation permit for the Bird Creek side, plus the Mount Adams Climbing Pass above 7,000 ft on national forest land
from.where: Buy the Tract D permit at the fee station where the road enters the reservation; the area is open to non-tribal visitors only in summer, roughly July to September. The Climbing Pass is sold on Recreation.gov.

to.what: Yakama Nation Tract D recreation permit for the Bird Creek side, plus the Mount Adams Climbing Pass above 7,000 ft on national forest land
to.where: Pay the Tract D fee at the fee box at Mirror Lake (cash or check); the area is open to non-tribal visitors only during a short summer window the Yakama Nation sets each year. The Climbing Pass is sold on Recreation.gov.
